summary: Iteration 42 — CRM Finance > Eficácia das Tarefas (Dashboard). Backend 15/15 pytest PASSED covering structure, filters (date/task_type/status/segment/feedback_reason), rate math (divide-by-zero safety + consistency), permissions (OWNER sees all, COLLECTIONS_AGENT auto-scoped, no-finance-role 403, unauth 401/403) and regression (/tasks/today + /clients-export). Frontend page /finance/tasks-effectiveness renders correctly for OWNER with all 20 data-testids present, filters interactive, refresh button works, no runtime errors. Menu visibility + access-control inconsistency noted (see action_items).

issues: React hydration console warnings: '<span> cannot be a child of <tbody>' and '<tr> cannot be a child of <span>'. Same root cause already reported in iteration_41 (data-ve-dynamic tooling span wrapping table rows). Not blocking, but persists on this new page's <table> because it uses the same <tbody>/<tr> pattern.

action_items: (Consistency) Menu 'Eficácia Tarefas' is gated on roles ['ADMIN','SUPERVISOR'] in Layout.js:217, but the route (App.js:229) and backend endpoint use requireFinanceAccess/require_finance_access. Result: COLLECTIONS_AGENT (role=AGENT, finance_role=COLLECTIONS_AGENT) CANNOT see the menu item but CAN access the URL directly and the API returns 200 with data auto-scoped to self. Either (a) widen menu to roles ['ADMIN','SUPERVISOR','AGENT'] and rely on backend for finance_role check (matches other finance menu items pattern), or (b) tighten the route to require ADMIN/SUPERVISOR only. Recommend (a) since backend already forces assigned_to=self for agents — this is the intended UX per the review-request note.
(Non-blocking / pre-existing) The <span data-ve-dynamic> tooling wrapper still produces hydration warnings around <tbody>/<tr> — also flagged in iteration_41 on FinanceClients.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py tasks_effectiveness: `block_suggestions = totals.get('done', 0)` on line 2949 is unused (never returned) and its comment '# aproximação a partir de task_type' is misleading. Safe to delete.

routes.py tasks_effectiveness: `mode` query param is accepted but never actually used inside the aggregation (only echoed back in filters.mode). Either wire it to filter finance_tasks (mode field on task) or drop the parameter.

routes.py tasks_effectiveness: total_promised_amount does an extra `db.finance_promises.find(promises_q, {'_id':0,'amount':1})` iteration on top of `count_documents`. Consider a single Mongo `$group` aggregation `[{$match: promises_q},{$group:{_id:null,total:{$sum:'$amount'},count:{$sum:1}}}]` to avoid two network round-trips.

routes.py tasks_effectiveness: dictionary lookup `totals[st] = totals.get(st, 0) + 1` accepts any unknown status silently and inserts it as a new key alongside the fixed schema (which promises 8 fields). If a task has status='foo' this would leak into totals. Consider whitelisting statuses.

routes.py tasks_effectiveness: iterates all matching tasks in memory (`async for t in db.finance_tasks.find(q)`); at 100k+ tasks this becomes O(N) work per request. For a dashboard, this is fine now but consider pre-computing daily rollups on tasks state transitions.
TasksEffectiveness.js: no error state UI (only console.error). If the API returns 500, the user sees an empty dashboard with no explanation. Add a `errorMsg` state + toast/banner.

TasksEffectiveness.js: `useCallback` deps include `getAuthHeaders` — if AuthContext returns a new object on every render, this re-fetches every render. Verify or wrap headers in useMemo in AuthContext.
TasksEffectiveness.js: `todayIso()` used in JSX ('Resumo diário — {todayIso()}') is recomputed on every render — negligible, but stylistically inconsistent with the const-based filter defaults.
